title: Session of First Presbyterian Church, Stanley, North Carolina v. Central Carolina Presbytery
disposition_detail: The General Assembly sustained complaint items 1, 2, and 5 and did not sustain items 3, 4, and 6. It instructed Presbytery to receive and hear the complaints under proper procedures and adopted recommendations admonishing better recordkeeping and encouraging pastoral oversight.
first_summary: The Session challenged Presbytery’s refusal to receive complaints and related voting, executive-session, elder-emeritus, interpretive, and disciplinary actions. The General Assembly sustained items 1, 2, and 5, but not items 3, 4, and 6. It directed Presbytery to receive and hear the complaints properly, upheld executive session and the elder emeritus’s voting privileges, and found item 6 improper in this court.
summary: The Session challenged Presbytery’s refusal to receive complaints and associated voting, executive-session, elder-emeritus, interpretive, and disciplinary actions. The General Assembly sustained items 1, 2, and 5, but not 3, 4, and 6. Receiving a complaint under BCO 43-1 was not subject to a vote; when heard, complainants and respondents could not participate. Executive session was permissible, an elder emeritus retained full privileges, and item 6 was improper in this court. No reason was given for item 5. Presbytery was instructed to receive and hear the complaints properly.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: The commission identified the proceeding as Case 6; its report was accepted as the General Assembly’s action and judgment, and the report as a whole was adopted (lines 29–33, 62–64; printed pp. 111–12).
evidence_notes.dispute: The filing challenged Presbytery’s refusal to hear complaints and actions involving voting, executive session, an elder emeritus, BCO 11-3, and alleged failures under BCO 27-5 and 46-5 (lines 15–19; printed p. 58).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Items 1, 2, and 5 were sustained; items 3, 4, and 6 were not. Reasons are stated for items 1–4 and 6, but not item 5 (lines 40–54; printed p. 111).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The adopted report also admonished Presbytery about recordkeeping and encouraged pastoral oversight; these were recommendations, not additional complaint specifications (lines 56–62; printed p. 111).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No separate decision was incorporated by reference. The judgment cited BCO provisions and Robert’s Rules as authority (lines 42–54; printed p. 111).

source_limits: The supplied source omits the attached complaints and gives no reasoning for sustaining item 5, limiting any fuller account of that issue.

score_reasons.concrete_dispute: Identifies the refusal to receive complaints and each associated category of challenge.
score_reasons.decision: States all six item-level outcomes and the instruction to Presbytery.
score_reasons.decisive_reason: Gives every stated reason and expressly notes the absence of a reason for item 5.
score_reasons.distinctive_value: Preserves the distinction between receiving a complaint without a vote and excluding parties when it is heard.
score_reasons.fidelity: Separates allegations, adopted rulings, operative instructions, and recommendations.
score_reasons.economy: Retains only details needed to understand the mixed result and practical consequence.

verification_notes: Rechecked the Assembly’s adoption, all six item-level dispositions, and the instruction to receive and hear complaints. The final summary adds the distinction between receipt and hearing participation and expressly notes that no reason was supplied for item 5.
